ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all subscribers, directors, officers, and UBOs against: (1) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List administered under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (2) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List (ISIL/Da'esh and Al-Qaida sanctions regime); (3) the OFAC SDN and Consolidated Non-SDN Lists for any USD Swift wire payment rails; (4) the Financial Action Task Force high-risk and monitored jurisdiction list; and (5) FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) guidance under PCMLTFA s 11.1 and SOR/2002-184. The screening output must be timestamped, evidenced, and retained for at least five years from the date of the last business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services / BC Corporate Online (bcregistry.ca) administered by the BC Registrar of Companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A British Columbia business corporation name must be in English or French (or a combination) using the Latin alphabet; any foreign-script name or transliteration must appear, in Latin-alphabet form, consistently in the Notice of Articles and Articles. Every name must comprise (i) a distinctive element, (ii) an optional descriptive element, and (iii) one of the mandated legal elements: Limited, Incorporated, Corporation, or a permitted abbreviation (Ltd., Inc., Corp., Ltée, etc.), per Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, s 2 and BC Reg 20/2002. A bilingual name may connect elements with 'and', '&', or 'et'. The registrar evaluates distinctiveness and potential confusion against all existing BC and federal corporate names, reserved names, and registered trade-marks.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Banking, Trust, Trust Company, Loan, Loan Company, Insurance, Assurance (requires federal approval under the Bank Act or Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions)
Barrister, Solicitor, Attorney, Legal Counsel, Notary, Notary Public (requires consent of the Law Society of British Columbia or Society of Notaries Public of British Columbia)
Architect, Engineer, Professional Engineer, Surveyor (requires certification by the respective professional association under the Professionals Act)
College, University, Institute, Academy (requires prior approval of the Ministry of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills)

Canada, Canadian, Royal, Empire, Commonwealth (requires written approval of federal authorities; 'British Columbia' or 'BC' used as a distinctive element may be rejected as misleading without provincial consent)
Cooperative, Co-op (limited to cooperatives incorporated under the Cooperative Association Act, SBC 1999, c 11)

Brewery, Brewpub, Beer, Malt, Distillery, Liquor, Wine, Cider, Cannabis, Pub, Retail liquor (triggers mandatory consultation with the Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch (LCRB) under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act and may require prior LCRB license eligibility before name confirmation)
Underground, Mine, Mining, Oil, Gas, Petroleum (requires regulatory consent or creates an impression of regulated mining/energy activity)
Any name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing corporate name, reserved name, or registered trade-mark contrary to s 2(2) of the Act
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A BC name reservation is valid for 56 days and may be extended for additional 56-day periods by filing an extension with BC Registries and paying the prescribed fee. If the registrar refuses the proposed name, the incorporator or authorized agent must, within 30 days of the refusal, submit a formal written reconsideration request to the BC Registrar of Companies citing s 22 of the Business Corporations Act, accompanied by: (1) the original name request number and the refusal notice; (2) written consent from the holder of a conflicting name or trade-mark, if obtainable; and (3) a distinctiveness memorandum demonstrating that the rejected name is not identical or confusingly similar given the first element and the goods/services of the applicant. If the registrar upholds the refusal, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c 241, within 60 days of the decision. A new name reservation may be filed concurrently without affecting the applicant's standing to appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the statutory registered office only, provided the address is a real, physical street location within British Columbia, staffed or acceptant of legal service during normal business hours, and is not described solely as a post office box (SBC 2002, c 57, s 35(2)). For the commercial substance of a craft beer distribution entity, a purely virtual address will not satisfy the Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch (LCRB) licensing requirement for a physical licensed distribution/storage premises, nor will it produce sufficient evidence of place of supply for GST/HST and excise purposes under the Excise Act, 2001. Accordingly, virtual office is accepted for the head office/registered office element; physical licensed premises are mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Less than 10% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection at the registered virtual office where a licensed corporate service agent is used; between 85% and 100% likelihood within the first 12 months of licensure for the LCRB-licensed distribution premises, which are subject to mandatory compliance inspections, plus Canada Revenue Agency excise verifications and Canada Border Services Agency customs audits for export clearance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, ss 4, 10, 11, 52; Companies Forms Regulation, BC Reg 56/2004
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Corporate and Property Registry, Ministry of Finance (Corporate Online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (Form 1) and Notice of Articles (Form 2) under the Companies Forms Regulation, BC Reg 56/2004
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Act permits any lawful share consideration. The authorized structure for this entity comprises an unlimited number of common shares issued to the incorporator in exchange for CAD 1,000 in working capital. No escrow deposit or capital withholding is mandated for a standard provincial incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that the filing of the Application for Incorporation and Notice of Articles via BC Corporate Online is ratified; that the registered office be established at [address], British Columbia, and corporate records maintained there; that the authorized share structure consisting of one class of unlimited common shares be confirmed, and 1,000 common shares be issued to the incorporator at par in consideration of CAD 1,000 of paid working capital, with no escrow required under the Business Corporations Act; that the directors and officers named in the Notice of Articles be appointed with standard borrowing, leasing, and contracting authorities; and that management be authorized to open bank accounts and pursue liquor, municipal, and environmental permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services, Corporate Online / NUANS Search Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into BC Corporate Online using a registered Business BCeID, commission a NUANS report for the proposed corporate name, and verify the name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing provincial or federal register entries. If name locking is required while drafting articles, submit a Name Reservation Request, which will reserve the name for 56 days.
required_dossiers: NUANS Search Report
Name Reservation Request form (where applicable)
BCeID credentials and applicant identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar objects on grounds of confusing similarity, refile with a revised name, obtain written consent from existing name rights holders, or submit a reconsideration request through Corporate Online within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles, Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the draft Articles and complete Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) and Form 2 (Notice of Articles). The Notice must state the registered office street address and the names, addresses, and consent of initial directors. Complete the director consent forms, confirm the authorized share structure, and ensure that the registered office is a physical BC address rather than a post office box.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles incorporating the BC Standard Articles as applicable
Form 1 Application for Incorporation
Form 2 Notice of Articles
Director Consent to Act forms
Registered office address verification (lease or property ownership evidence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency query under s 10 of the Business Corporations Act, correct the notice, re-execute affected signature pages, and submit a supplementary affidavit or amended form within 14 days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Online (BC Registrar of Companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the completed incorporation documents electronically through BC Corporate Online, remit the CAD 350 statutory filing fee, and download the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval. The Certificate is conclusive evidence of incorporation and, with the filed Notice of Articles, forms the company's foundational instrument.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 1 and Form 2
Valid NUANS report identifier / name reservation reference
Payment authorization (credit card, BCeID invoice, or corporate debit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the electronic application is rejected due to validation errors, obtain the system Error Report, correct the data fields, and resubmit. If rejected on substantive grounds, cure by filing a fresh application or seek judicial review of the Registrar's refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and BC Ministry of Finance (eTaxBC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the federal Business Number using CRA Business Registration Online and simultaneously register for the GST/HST account, import/export accounts, and payroll deductions accounts as applicable. Register for provincial sales tax (PST) through eTaxBC and enroll with WorkSafeBC for workers' compensation coverage effective upon the first employee hire.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and filed Notice of Articles
Directors' and officers' personal identification details
RC1 Request for a Business Number form
Proof of business premises lease
Bank account details for operating accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application is rejected or delayed, call the CRA Business Enquiries line (1-800-959-5525) to complete manual registration; incorrect PST or GST registrations may be amended through eTaxBC within 90 days with statutory penalty relief if filed voluntarily.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Zoning and Fire Department Clearance for Physical Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality planning division and municipal fire rescue department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the lease agreement, site plan, and certificate of incorporation to the municipality to obtain a zoning determination confirming that a keg distribution center and support cold-chain warehouse are permitted uses on the premises. Arrange a fire inspection to obtain an Occupancy Permit confirming compliance with the BC Fire Code, including fire separation, sprinkler protection, egress, and emergency lighting. Have a certified professional verify the structural adequacy of floors designated for refrigerated keg storage.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the cold-chain keg warehouse
Site plan showing egress paths and hazardous storage areas
Sprinkler system installation certificate
Zoning compliance letter from municipality
Structural load assessment signed by a licensed professional engineer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection identifies deficiencies, receive a corrective action report, complete prescribed remedial works, and schedule re-inspection within the order period; a denied occupancy permit may be appealed to the municipal building appeals board.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch (LCRB), Ministry of Public Safety and Solicitor General, Government of British Columbia; with federal coordination through the Canada Revenue Agency Excise Duty Licensing Unit under the Excise Act, 2001
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Craft Brewery Manufacturer's Licence for Distribution and Export (BC LCRB); Federal Excise Warehouse Licence for Beer (EA2001); Municipal Business Licence for Keg Wholesale and Cold-Chain Storage

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Environmental Protection Division (with municipal discharge authorizations administered by Metro Vancouver)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-level discharge authorization, not a full Environmental Assessment; the microbrewery distribution operation falls below full EIA triggers under the Environmental Assessment Act and is treated as a low-risk trade waste discharging facility subject to a municipal sewerage discharge permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Brewery wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must meet Metro Vancouver discharge standards: pH 6.0-11.0, BOD5 equal to or below 300 mg/L, TSS below 350 mg/L, total phosphorus below 10 mg/L, temperature equal to or below 65°C; fermentation vent VOCs must remain below 6 t/annum; spent grain, spent yeast, and packaging waste shall be removed by licensed waste carriers to approved composting or rendering facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy Permit issued following municipal fire inspection under the BC Fire Code and British Columbia Building Code (F-2 industrial classification); structural load clearance for keg racks and refrigerated cold-storage floors signed by a licensed professional engineer; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance with employer payroll registration effective upon first hire.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - federal administrator of corporate income tax, GST/HST, and excise duties under the Excise Act, 2001; CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (MyBA) are the principal registration and filing portals. Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers export/import declarations through the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) platform and the Canadian International Trade Single Window. The British Columbia Ministry of Finance, BC Revenue Division (eTaxBC), administers BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST), Employer Health Tax (EHT), and municipal/regional district tax levies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate as a business corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) via Corporations Canada or under the BC Business Corporations Act (BCBCA) via BC Registries; comply with resident-director requirements (CBCA requires at least 25% of directors to be resident Canadians, with a minimum of one resident Canadian director where the board has fewer than four directors; BCBCA generally requires at least one director who is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident ordinarily resident in Canada unless an exemption applies). Step 2: Register with CRA for a nine-digit federal Business Number (BN) using Business Registration Online or Form RC1; the BN functions as the corporate income tax account number and as the base for program accounts, including the GST/HST account (BN plus RT suffix and four digits), the payroll account, and the importer/exporter account (BN plus RM suffix). Step 3: Register with the BC Revenue Division through eTaxBC for PST before making any taxable sale or lease in British Columbia; no monetary registration threshold applies for PST. Step 4: Register for BC EHT if the employer's BC remuneration exceeds the applicable statutory exemption threshold, currently the first CAD 500,000 of BC remuneration for employers above the threshold. Step 5: Obtain the federal excise brewery licence and the provincial liquor licence from the BC Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch (LCRB) for manufacturing and wholesale distribution of craft beer. Step 6: Activate the CBSA importer/exporter account via CARM to file B13A export declarations and, where applicable, excise duty drawback or exportation relief claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a CBCA or BCBCA business corporation is a resident of Canada when it is incorporated in Canada or when its central management and control is situated in Canada; it is a separate taxpayer under section 2 of the Income Tax Act (ITA), subject to federal Part I corporate income tax and BC provincial corporate income tax on income attributable to a BC permanent establishment. No flow-through, partnership, or check-the-box classification is available for a Canadian corporation. A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada is taxable under ITA section 2(3) on Canadian-source income and, on ceasing to carry on business, may be exposed to the 25% branch tax under ITA section 219, subject to treaty reduction. The entity is not a Tax_Exempt_Zone entity and is taxed on worldwide income, so Canada is not a pure Territorial_Scope jurisdiction for corporations resident in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a domestic check-the-box election; foreign entity classification follows CRA administrative policy (Income Tax Folio S4-F1-C1), which looks to de jure legal personality and limited liability, and hybrid mismatch arrangements are addressed legislatively under ITA sections 18.4 to 18.6, consistent with BEPS Action 2 and the Multilateral Instrument. Available elections relevant to the licensed craft beer distributor include: (i) ITA section 85 rollover election to transfer eligible property into the corporation on incorporation; (ii) GST/HST section 156 election to treat closely related corporations as a single person for VAT simplification; (iii) GST/HST section 167 election to apply no tax on a transfer of a business as a going concern; (iv) ETA section 240(3) election for a small supplier to register voluntarily so as to claim input tax credits; (v) election to use the GST/HST Quick Method where the distributorship qualifies; (vi) BC PST purchase-for-resale exemption, evidenced by a valid PST resale certificate issued by the BC Revenue Division, so that no PST is charged on wholesale keg and packaged beer supplies; and (vii) excise duty exportation or drawback elections under the Excise Act, 2001 for beer removed for export.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Excise Tax Act (ETA), with the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applicable only in participating provinces; British Columbia applies the federal GST at 5% and does not apply HST. The BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) is a separate retail sales and use tax at 7% applicable to retail sales of goods in BC, and alcoholic beverages are additionally subject to the federal Excise Act, 2001 excise duty regime; the combined headline consumer tax burden on taxable retail goods in British Columbia is therefore 12% (5% GST plus 7% PST), with PST not applying to goods for resale by licensed distributors or to goods shipped outside BC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - a person carrying on business in Canada, including a non-resident corporation, must register for GST/HST once the value of its worldwide taxable supplies exceeds CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA section 240; small supplier rules); a non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada through a substantial physical or digital presence in Canada is also subject to GST/HST. BC PST registration has no monetary threshold, while BC Employer Health Tax applies only where BC remuneration exceeds the statutory exemption threshold currently set at CAD 500,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), digital stamping, or government pre-clearance for GST/HST invoices. Electronic invoicing is legally valid, but the ETA requires invoices to contain prescribed information and supporting input tax credit documentation. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE, MyBA, or a CRA-certified service provider), with mandatory electronic filing for registrants filing under prescribed categories; business records, including invoices, export evidence, and excise drawback files, must be retained for at least six years. Exports are subject to mandatory electronic customs reporting with CBSA through CARM, including the B13A Export Declaration, e-manifest, or an authorized Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) / Single Window equivalent; BC PST exemption certificates and excise duty records must also be retained for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, item 1, a supply of tangible personal property is zero-rated where the property is exported from Canada as part of the supply, is delivered to a destination outside Canada, and the supplier retains proof of export; kegs of artisanal hazy IPA sold by the licensed distributor to US or other foreign consignees therefore bear GST at 0%. Services supplied to non-residents that are not performed for consumption in Canada and are unrelated to Canadian real estate or tangible property are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, items 6 and 7. The supplier must obtain contemporaneous documentary proof of export and keep it in its books and records for the statutory six-year retention period; CRA will recharacterize the supply as taxable if credible proof is not available at audit. BC PST does not apply to goods delivered to a destination outside British Columbia, and a valid resale certificate removes PST on wholesale sales to licensed BC customers. Beer exported by a licensed brewery is relieved from federal excise duty under the Excise Act, 2001, and if excise duty was already paid at removal, a drawback claim may be filed upon proof of exportation. Canada does not impose a general statutory 180-day deadline for repatriation of export proceeds; the 180-day benchmark is retained in this dossier as the prudent evidentiary ceiling for bank receipts, SWIFT payments, and foreign-exchange documentation supporting zero-rating claims and transfer-pricing consistency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: B13A Export Declaration or CBSA-approved electronic equivalent filed through the CARM / Canadian International Trade Single Window system
Commercial invoice and customs valuation documentation, including HS classification and, where relevant, a CUSMA certificate of origin for North American markets
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or equivalent multimodal transport document evidencing shipment to the foreign consignee and the foreign destination
Container, keg, and brewery lot records demonstrating physical removal of the beer from Canada and identifying the export shipment
Inward remittance evidence comprising bank foreign-exchange confirmation, SWIFT MT103, or equivalent payment record matching the invoice value, currency, and due date
Excise Act, 2001 drawback claim or exportation relief documentation where beer was duty-paid at removal, together with the warehouse or export-premises removal authority
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess GST/HST within four years of a return, extended to seven years in the case of neglect, misrepresentation, or attributable to a not-at-arm's-length person, and with no limitation period where fraud or wilful default is established. False zero-rating claims, circular export invoicing, fabricated bills of lading, or unrepatriated proceeds that reveal unreported income may trigger: (i) GST/HST false-statement penalties under ETA section 285(1) equal to the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax sought to be evaded; (ii) GST/HST failure-to-file and failure-to-register penalties, including amounts under ETA section 280(1); (iii) gross-negligence penalties of 50% of understated federal income tax under ITA section 163(2), with analogous BC provincial penalty provisions; (iv) daily compound interest at prescribed rates on all reassessed net tax and income tax, with recovery of previously allowed input tax credits and refunds; (v) denial or vacation of the zero-rating treatment and export drawback where proof of export is not substantiated, causing the supply to be recharacterized as taxable in Canada; (vi) director and officer liability for unremitted GST/HST and excise duty under the ETA and Excise Act, 2001; (vii) criminal prosecution for evasion under ETA section 327 and ITA section 239, punishable on summary conviction by fines ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to two years less a day, and on indictment by fines ranging from 100% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years; and (viii) CBSA administrative monetary penalties (AMPS) under the Customs Act of up to CAD 25,000 per false declaration, export-data penalty, or contravention, plus seizure or detention of goods. CRA may claw back refunds claimed beyond the limitation period and apply general anti-avoidance, sham, or substance doctrines to reverse zero-rating benefits obtained without real exportation and genuine foreign receipt of payment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); oversight of the Crown’s Exchange Fund Account and foreign-exchange reserves rests with the Minister of Finance under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act. Canada maintains an independently floating exchange-rate regime and has no exchange-control law or central-bank approval requirement for cross-border payments. AML/FX dealer oversight is exercised by FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA and by OSFI for deposit-taking institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Canada is an IMF Article VIII member; no restrictions exist on dividend, interest, royalty, or capital repatriation by foreign-owned Canadian subsidiaries. Inbound equity for the BC distribution entity requires only a post-establishment notification under section 12 of the Investment Canada Act (greenfield), not a prior review. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is subject to Part XIII withholding tax – generally 25%, reducible to 5% on qualifying treaty dividends (e.g., US-Canada Treaty Article X). No BC provincial exchange controls apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation obligation for export proceeds. The CAD is free-float; exporters may retain USD in on-shore or offshore accounts. Customs export declarations (B13A) serve statistical and trade-security purposes only. Upon conversion, foreign-exchange gains/losses are recognized for CIT under section 39 of the Income Tax Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: CAD Operating Account + USD Cross-Border Clearing Sub-Account (RBC Georgia N.A. corridor)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Montreal (BMO Bank of Montreal)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Contribution Escrow Account (USD) + CAD Operational Account; BMO Harris N.A. USD corridor
CAD Commercial Operating Account with standalone 'TD U.S. Dollar' Daily Interest Account
Business Operating Account + CIBC US Dollar Account with overnight sweep
Business Banking Core Account + global trade services desk for LC and collection
Commercial Operating Account and FX/hedging treasury line (Pacific region Vancouver office)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium – viable only as a supplementary collections/disbursement rail, not as the primary treasury account. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Payoneer) operating into Canada must register with FINTRAC as a foreign money services business (MSB) and are not licensed deposit-taking institutions capable of taking the regulated USD capital contribution. Canadian Schedule I banks remain the legally required receptacle for the parent capital injection and for LCRB/Excise-compliance operational cash-flow controls.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINTRAC imposes no statutory requirement for physical presence; identity verification may be conducted remotely using a credit-file check plus a valid government-issued ID for Canadian-resident signatories (RBC, BMO, TD support fully digital onboarding). A non-resident sole director/UBO triggers a formal 'non-face-to-face' EDD protocol: notarized/certified passport, apostilled corporate registry extract, and either a scheduled video call with the branch compliance officer or, where the bank declines video, one in-person interview at the Vancouver Commercial Banking Centre. Appointing a Canadian-resident officer with a banking resolution as co-signatory removes the physical-attendance impediment for all Big Six banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated zero-history federal/BC corporation with minimal share capital and no prior regulatory licence history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation (CBCA or BC BCA), Notice of Articles/By-laws, board resolution approving account mandate, detailed business plan with 12-month revenue projection, executed distribution agreements with BC Liquor Distribution Branch and US wholesalers, proof of the federal Excise Duty Brewer's Licence and BC LCRB Wholesale Liquor Licence, plus parent company audited financials for the prior fiscal year.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO and nominee-director structures triggering EDD: PEP/sanctions screening hits via World-Check, FATF jurisdictional flags, or ultimate ownership opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain-of-ownership chart to natural persons; certified passport copies apostilled/legalized in the UBO jurisdiction; independent source-of-funds letter from a licensed foreign CPA; certificate of non-residency for Part XIII purposes; parent corporate guarantee; signed PEP self-certification; confirmation that neither the UBO nor the financing chain appears on OSFI/UN/OFAC sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Operational red flag: high-frequency USD inflows concentrated from a narrow group of US craft-beer wholesalers with rapid onward disbursement to hop/malt suppliers (looks like pass-through/structuring)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed US distribution and supply contracts, customer concentration explanation memo, EDC export-credit insurance policy evidencing trade repayment integrity, dedicated USD sub-account structure to segregate settlement funds, pre-set daily disbursement limits, board-approved cash-management policy, and prior-bank reference letter from the beneficial owner's legacy institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Protocol: parent initiates a SWIFT MT103 USD wire to the Canadian bank's Vancouver commercial branch. Field 23B = CRED; Field 50F = parent company; Field 59 = named beneficiary entity [CA_CORP]; Field 70 = 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – INVESTMENT CANADA ACT GREENFIELD NOTIFICATION NO. ICA-2025-XXXX'; Field 71A = OUR. Pre-funding conditions: bank-approved board resolution, executed subscription agreement, and notice filed under section 12 of the Investment Canada Act. Verification: Treasury Operations matches the reference to the onboarding capital plan; the amount is deposited into the USD Capital Escrow Account and released to the Operating Account solely upon completion of EDD acceptance of the source-of-funds file (parent audited statements). Cash amounts above CAD 10,000 trigger FINTRAC LCTR reporting; wire amounts require STR reporting only if suspicion arises.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier settlements (US hops, malt, keg inventory), with Field 70 citing the underlying invoice and B13A export declaration where applicable. Secondary rail: commercial letters of credit issued by the Vancouver trade-services desk for high-value bulk-glass/keg purchases; documentary collections (D/P or D/A) available for established counterparties. Domestic rail: Canadian Payments Association EFT/Pre-authorized Debits for BC liquor store and restaurant settlements, with USD receipts cleared via the bank's US correspondent network (RBC Georgia, BMO Harris, TD Bank NA) directly into the segregated USD sub-account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/CAD forward contract (up to 24 months, collateralized under the bank's standard FX master agreement)
FX swap (USD/CAD) for temporary liquidity bridging between sales-settlement and tariff-payment dates
Cross-currency interest rate swap (USD/CAD) applicable to the parent's intercompany financing facility
Vanilla FX call and put options (USD/CAD) for risk reversal strategies on large seasonal export contracts

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) only for offshore counterparty scenarios where physical CAD delivery is unavailable; NDFs are permissible but operationally disfavoured for onshore CAD as CAD is fully deliverable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (AR-BC) under Business Corporations Act s.273 - standard filing fee CAD 37.70
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies - Corporate Registry, BC Ministry of Finance (BC Registry Online)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 2 months after fiscal year end; if no fiscal year end declared, within 2 months after each incorporation anniversary. Example: FYE Dec 31 = deadline Feb 28 next year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late-filing penalty; Certificate of Good Standing blocked; two consecutive missed Annual Reports trigger administrative strike-off and dissolution under BCBCA s.274

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Significant Individuals UBO Annual Confirmation - BC Transparency Register Declaration embedded in the BC Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies - Transparency Register (BC Registry Online)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as BC Annual Report (within 2 months after fiscal year end); any intervening UBO change must be filed within 10 business days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and officers exposed to BCBCA offence fines; incomplete Transparency Declaration invalidates the Annual Report and triggers the full Annual Report late-filing and strike-off chain

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal Part I plus BC provincial corporate income tax, both administered by CRA under tax collection agreement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed within 6 months after fiscal year end; tax balance due within 2 months after FYE for non-CCPCs and 3 months after FYE for CCPCs claiming the small business deduction. Example: FYE Dec 31 = T2 due Jun 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; daily prescribed compound arrears interest; repeated-failure penalty; director liability for unremitted withholdings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (annual filing permitted when taxable supplies < CAD 1.5M)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year end for annual filers; quarterly instalments due one month after each calendar quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of unremitted net tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; prescribed daily compounded interest; minimum penalty assessments for late nil returns

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Ministry of Finance - Consumer Taxation Branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the month following each reporting period (monthly, quarterly, or annually as assigned by PST liability size)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing penalty on unremitted PST plus prescribed interest; additional 2% penalty if tax remains unpaid 60 days after assessment; collection and director liability under BC Tax Administration Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Liquor Wholesale Licence Annual Renewal (including LCLB financial and surety attestation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch (LCLB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before licence expiry; LCLB renewal window opens 60 days prior to expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Wholesale distribution of beer without a current licence is an offence under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act; fines up to CAD 100,000, product seizure, licence suspension or cancellation, and strike-off of the entity's vendor eligibility

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under BCBCA, a statutory auditor is mandatory only for public companies (listed/traded securities); a private BC corporation may avoid auditor appointment if all shareholders consent by unanimous resolution each year. LCLB may require an independent accountant's review engagement for higher-volume liquor wholesalers, and CRA can impose audited financial statements for large GST/liquor excise accountholders (typically taxable supplies above CAD 10M).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook - IFRS for reporting issuers; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for this private BC corporation; CRA tax reporting on accrual basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BCBCA Transparency Register requires filing Significant Individuals UBO data with the Registrar; the annual confirmation is embedded in the BC Annual Report; any share transfer or change of control creating a new significant individual must be updated in the in-house register and filed with the Registrar within 10 business days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Significant Individuals - UBO Transparency Register (BCBCA s.119.1)
Minute Book (shareholder and board meeting records)
Central Securities Register (if multiple share classes or series)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110-420 per year (typical BC registered and records office agent annual fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-30,000 (review engagement CAD 5,000-12,000; full audit CAD 18,000-40,000 depending on revenue and LCLB/CRA scope)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined (15% federal Part I general rate + 12% British Columbia general corporate rate); non-resident-owned or public corporations are denied the CAD 500,000 small-business threshold
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: Canadian-controlled private corporations pay 9% federal + 2% BC provincial = 11% combined on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income earned in BC; SR&ED investment tax credits (35% refundable federal credit for qualifying expenditures up to CAD 3,000,000 and 10% refundable BC credit); 20-year non-capital loss carryforward reduces effective rate of profitable years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (2016+) filed with the Canada Revenue Agency through EFILE / Corporate Internet Filing (no paper mandate for tax preparers); Schedule 125 (GIFI) and Schedule 141 (T2 summary) integrated; BC provincial return is Form T2BC filed electronically with the T2 package.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (every fiscal period regardless of whether tax is payable)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (ITA subsection 150(1)); balance-due date is 3 months after year-end for Canadian-controlled private corporations and 2 months for other corporations; large corporations with existing instalment obligations pay quarterly instalments under ITA section 157.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) before tax as reconciled from financial statements: craft beer inventory, keg deposits, cold-chain freight cost of sales, and excise duty expense reported as part of the income-statement mapping.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned corporations must file the same GIFI data and additionally identify cross-border purchases of unfermented malt extract, hops and marketing intangibles in the 'intercompany transactions' flag fields.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adding back 50% of meals and entertainment, non-deductible expenses, fines, and after deducting non-capital loss carryforwards and prior-year foreign tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply subsections 111(1) and 18(1)(b); treaty-protected business income must be excluded from the taxable-income line only where a permanent establishment is absent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 (Part I Tax at statutory rates; federal abatement and general rate reduction)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax computed as 38% of taxable income less the 10% provincial abatement and the 13% general rate reduction, producing a 15% federal rate; Schedule 7 is used to claim the Small Business Deduction reducing active business income by an additional 6 percentage points.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No Small Business Deduction (Schedule 7) is available to a corporation that is not Canadian-controlled; only the 15% general federal rate is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 (Federal tax otherwise payable; SR&ED credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Craft brewing applied-research and cold-chain innovation expenditures eligible for the 35% refundable SR&ED credit for CCPCs; any refundable credits are entered with their income inclusion adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-CCPC non-resident-owned corporations claim only the 15% non-refundable federal SR&ED credit; foreign-owned corporations must allocate expenditures to Canadian bookkeeping records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 15 (Part I tax payable; RDTOH and refundable dividend tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The Schedule 53 refundable dividend tax on hand calculation adds 38.33% of aggregate investment income to the refundable account; beer distribution profits qualify as active business income only when no associated corporation exceeds the CAD 500,000 threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned corporation entirely earning treaty-protected passive income is exempt from Part I tax but must file the T2 return and Part XIII reporting with Schedule 91.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory identification of each non-resident shareholder, jurisdiction of residence, share class, ownership percentage and aggregate dividends paid during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder must annex its Certificate of Residence (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for the U.S.) to the Schedule 91 documentation file to support treaty withholding relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial allocation of taxable income, 12% general provincial rate, 2% BC small business rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, and BC tax credits such as the BC Training Tax Credit and BC SR&ED Credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: BC provincial tax is collected at the CRA under the tax-collection agreement; a non-resident corporation must still compute BC taxable income (same base with provincial add-backs) if it has a permanent establishment in BC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; repeat failure within 3 years: 10% plus 2% per month; failure to report income penalty under section 163(2) of 50% of the understated tax for gross negligence; daily compound interest on unpaid balances at the CRA prescribed rate (approximately 8% in 2025-2026).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T106 Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents (electronically transmitted through CRA's internet filing)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; the T106 must be attached when the aggregate fair market value of all reportable non-arm's length cross-border transactions exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the taxation year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each cross-border transaction with a related non-resident party, including beer concentrate importation, IPA hop supply agreements, territorial expansion licensing, and management-cost recharges from a foreign affiliate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident vendors must be identified with their jurisdiction of tax residence and their relationship to the distributing shareholder; a transfer pricing policy memo must accompany each transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II – Transfer pricing method selection
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nomination of the arm's length method (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split) and contemporaneous benchmark study references.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder supplying proprietary brewing technology must demonstrate that the royalty rate is consistent with comparable licensing transactions in the craft beverage industry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule – Loss of T106 filing exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: If the transaction amount crosses the CAD 1,000,000 threshold, the corporation must complete all T106 schedules; no de minimis exemption exists once the threshold is exceeded for the full balance of a transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The CAD 1,000,000 test is measured per counter-party and in aggregate for the entire fiscal year; conversion of non-CAD invoicing is performed at the Bank of Canada monthly average rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file an accurate T106 attracts a penalty of CAD 50 per day up to a maximum of CAD 2,500 per return; where the omission is the result of gross negligence, a penalty of CAD 100 per day up to CAD 25,000 can be imposed under subsection 162(8).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax under Income Tax Act subsection 212(2) applies to any dividend or deemed dividend paid by a resident Canadian corporation to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder must deliver a current Certificate of Residence issued by its home tax authority to the Canadian payor prior to payment (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for the United States). The payor then applies the DTA rate at source; if 25% is nevertheless withheld, the shareholder files CRA Form NR7 (Application for Refund of Part XIII Withholding Tax) within two years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid. The Canada-US treaty reduces the source rate to 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% when the US beneficial owner is a corporation holding at least 10% of the Canadian corporation's voting shares. Other DTAs generally provide rates of 5% (substantial shareholding) or 15% (portfolio).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 25% on both royalties (subsection 212(1)(d)) and interest (subsection 212(1)(b)). Under the Canada-US Convention (Fifth Protocol): royalties and interest paid to US residents are generally exempt from Canadian source withholding (0%), with the sole exception of film/television royalties which remain taxable at 10%. Most other Canadian DTAs apply 10% to 15% for royalties and 10% to 15% for interest, subject to a 0%-rate for arm's-length interest in specific Australian, German, and Luxembourg treaties, and the no-withholding rule for arm's-length interest paid to US tax-exempt pension funds.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 of aggregate fair market value of non-arm's length cross-border transactions in a fiscal year triggers the mandatory filing of Form T106 and the expectation of a contemporaneous Local File; a Master File and country-by-country report are required only for MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least CAD 750 million, which does not ordinarily apply to a standalone microbrewery distributor.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not administer a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the Income Tax Act contains a general anti-avoidance rule (section 245) denying the tax benefit where a transaction is an avoidance transaction that misuses or abuses the Act and lacks real economic substance; the CRA also relies on beneficial-ownership analysis in the Canada-US treaty, the statutory anti-hybrid rules (subsections 18.2 and 18.5 of the Income Tax Regulations), and the global minimum tax laws under OECD Pillar Two for large groups. A BC craft-beer distribution entity must maintain physical inventory, transfer-pricing benchmarks, real distribution personnel and board minutes demonstrating commercial activity in Canada; otherwise, GAAR, gross-negligence penalty (section 163(2)) and, in egregious cases, criminal tax-evasion charges (section 239) apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly false T2 filing, unreported cash keg sales, fictitious export documentation for hazy IPAs, fabricated hop-supplier invoices, or wilfully suppressing inventory shrinkage to reduce income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 239: fine of 50% to 200% of the evaded federal income tax plus up to 5 years imprisonment on indictment; the Crown imposes civil penalties and full restitution under section 240; CRA may freeze bank accounts and take judgment collection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who direct, participate in, or acquiesce in the evasion are personally exposed to penal prosecution as parties to the offence; a conviction imposes the same fines, asset forfeiture under the Criminal Code, travel restrictions pending trial, and personal restitution orders that are not dischargeable in bankruptcy.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Installing a BC subsidiary with no cold-chain operations, no employees and no inventory solely to route royalty or commission income to a zero-tax jurisdiction and to claim the BC small-business rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 245 of the Income Tax Act recharacterizes transactions and denies the tax benefit; gross-negligence penalty under section 163(2) of 50% of the tax evaded applies when the taxpayer fails to exercise reasonable care; the related Schedule 125 GIFI misstatement can itself trigger a 50% false-statement penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under CBCA section 122(1), directors who approve a sham structure breach fiduciary duty and are civilly liable in oppression-remedy proceedings for resulting shareholder losses; the CRA can assert personal liability under section 227.1 for unpaid source deductions and, where fraud is established, courts will pierce the corporate veil and impose restitution against the natural persons.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing export sales of hazy IPA to a related US or Swiss distributor, overpaying a non-resident affiliate for proprietary yeast cultures, or charging no arm's length royalty for the foreign trademark, in the absence of contemporaneous TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Subsection 247(3) penalty: an amount equal to 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment (no de minimis floor once the adjustment is confirmed); adjustments are recomputed on the arm's length principle under subsection 247(2); CRA may also apply the 50% gross-negligence penalty under section 163(2) for deliberately omitted intercompany transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the T2 return with knowledge of the mispricing are exposed to the same criminal sanctions as the corporation under section 239; in practice CRA pursues the corporate entity first, but the section 227.1 director liability includes unremitted withholding on the cross-border royalty payments, and false testimonials at audit create personal exposure to the Criminal Code fraud offence (section 380) with penal conclusions of up to 14 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Excise Duty Evasion on Beer Production and Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a BC microbrewery licence without Canada Revenue Agency excise licence, under-declaring hectolitres produced, diverting duty-free raw material to on-premise retail, or marking duty-paid kegs as exported when they are sold domestically.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Excise Act, 2001 sections 100 and 214: a fine equal to the duty evaded plus an administrative penalty of 200% of the duty; for a criminal breach, imprisonment up to 5 years and confiscation of brewing equipment and stock; duty is a deemed Crown debt and survives the dissolution of the corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the licensed brewery are jointly and severally liable for unpaid excise duties and daily interest under the Excise Act, 2001; the classic 'director's plea' of personal liability is applied in the same way as source deductions — a director can be assessed without limiting statutory notice if the director knew or ought to have known of the duty liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Trade Sanctions, AML and FINTRAC Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large volumes of cash for craft beer deliveries from a non-resident intermediary, failing to report CAD 10,000+ cash transactions to FINTRAC, or maintaining an unregistered money-services-business mirror account in a sanctioned jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2,000,000 for a corporation found guilty of a serious violation; Criminal Code section 462.31 imposes imprisonment up to 10 years for laundering proceeds; Customs Act penalties apply on misdescribed export shipments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly omit the FINTRAC report or direct the cash-skimming operation are prosecuted as co-principals; criminal conviction triggers mandatory surrender of passports, the issuance of an international arrest warrant through Interpol, and personal civil restitution to the Crown; Canada prosecutes directors individually even where the corporate entity is insolvent.
